name: Sesamin
short: No serious adverse events in a 28-day study of sesamin plus episesamin in 48 healthy people. Interaction evidence is laboratory and rat data only.
text: In a placebo-controlled study in 48 healthy subjects randomised to 50 mg of sesame lignans (sesamin and episesamin) or placebo once daily for 28 days, no serious adverse events were observed and no accumulation was seen. Laboratory work shows that sesamin is metabolised mainly by the liver enzyme CYP2C9 and can inhibit it; in a follow-up rat study sesamin did not significantly change blood levels of the anti-inflammatory medicine diclofenac, and the authors concluded that no significant interaction occurs at standard supplement doses. This interaction evidence comes from laboratory and animal data, not from human studies.
